The story uses sophisticated metaphors to convey emotional truths: Josie understands her father’s world “as weather rather than fact,” suggesting intuitive awareness without explicit acknowledgment. Her effort to fit the “shape” of his life captures her self-conscious performance of maturity. His heartbeat, like someone persistently knocking at a door, makes his physical fragility and will to live palpable. These images deepen the story’s themes of belonging, impending loss, and care without stating them outright.
